content:
Optimizing Chemical Processes with Reliable Pump Solutions # The chemical industry encompasses a vast array of sectors, from small-scale operations to global conglomerates with intricate production systems. Despite this diversity, a common thread runs through all chemical applications: the need for robust, corrosion-resistant pumps capable of handling everything from aggressive acids and toxic chemicals to flammable solvents and explosive compounds. Ensuring safety and reliability is fundamental when selecting pumps for these demanding environments.
The Importance of Customization in Pump Solutions # Standard, off-the-shelf pumps often fall short in meeting the unique requirements of chemical processes. Customized pump solutions provide a significant advantage by addressing specific operational needs. Chemical processes are highly specialized, and the right pump selection is crucial for maintaining process stability, efficiency, and yield.
The customization process begins with thorough consultations to understand your system’s unique parameters, such as piping configuration and intended pump applications. By analyzing these factors, experts can calculate system resistance and Net Positive Suction Head available (NPSHa), ensuring the selected pump is perfectly matched to your requirements. This tailored approach not only optimizes performance but also extends equipment lifespan and maximizes operational efficiency.
Ensuring Reliability for Continuous Operation # Reliability is non-negotiable in chemical operations, where downtime directly impacts productivity and revenue. Several factors contribute to pump reliability:
Design and Standards: Pumps for chemical plants typically adhere to industry standards like ISO 2858, ISO 5199, ISO 15783, ANSI, or API, ensuring consistency and interchangeability. Performance Verification: Reliable pumps are backed by rigorous quality assurance and performance testing. An ILAC-accredited laboratory can provide certified performance data, and it is essential to verify that the pump’s NPSHr aligns with the system’s NPSHa to prevent premature failure. Comprehensive Testing: Even pumps not requiring ILAC certification undergo thorough hydraulic testing before delivery. Test data is archived and available for reference, supporting transparency and accountability. Simplifying Maintenance for Maximum Uptime # Maintenance efficiency plays a pivotal role in minimizing downtime. Easy-maintain pump solutions are designed for straightforward checkups and repairs:
User-Friendly Construction: Simple, close-coupled designs allow for back pull-out dismantling and rapid reassembly without special tools or time-consuming shaft alignment. Lined Pumps for Light-Duty Applications: Removable liners enable targeted repairs, reducing both costs and material waste by replacing only worn or damaged parts. Clear Maintenance Guidance: Instructional videos and resources support maintenance teams, ensuring tasks are completed efficiently and correctly. These features collectively reduce downtime, lower maintenance costs, and contribute to a reduced carbon footprint over the pump’s lifecycle.
Comprehensive Service and Support # Purchasing a pump is just the beginning. Ongoing service and support are essential for maintaining smooth operations and maximizing return on investment:
Localized Support: Regional service teams provide prompt assistance, minimizing downtime and ensuring timely maintenance, even for pumps purchased from other sources. Agile Supply Chain: Fast turnaround for parts and service keeps operations running smoothly. Flexible Maintenance Options: Choose between DIY maintenance or professional contractor support, depending on your needs and expertise. With comprehensive service and support, you can be confident that any pump-related issue will be addressed swiftly, keeping your processes flowing.
About ASSOMA # ASSOMA INC. specializes in the design and provision of industrial plastic chemical pumps, serving as a trusted partner to the chemical industry. The company operates an ILAC-certified performance test laboratory, offering testing services for pumps of any brand. ASSOMA’s global network of distributors and service agents ensures seamless support, regardless of where the pump was purchased. The company is committed to delivering value through high-efficiency pumps with advanced hydraulics, aiming to reduce energy consumption and lifecycle costs for chemical industry clients.
For more information or to discuss your specific requirements, contact us.

content:
Technological Advancements and Process Optimization in PCB Manufacturing # The Printed Circuit Board (PCB) industry has experienced rapid transformation in recent years, driven by the demand for smaller, more complex electronic devices. This article explores the evolution of PCB technology, the challenges faced in production, and the strategies manufacturers employ to optimize processes and remain competitive.
PCB Industry PCB Evolution The Role of PCBs in Modern Electronics # Printed Circuit Boards are fundamental to all electronic devices, serving as the backbone that connects components such as displays, batteries, memory, storage, modems, camera modules, and sensors. These elements are mounted onto the PCB, which provides the necessary electrical connections for integrated operation. As devices become more compact and powerful, PCB designs must accommodate increasingly dense and intricate circuits.
Evolution of PCB Technology # The development of PCBs has progressed from traditional single-sided, double-sided, and multi-layer boards—used in basic electronics like calculators and computer motherboards—to advanced high-density interconnect (HDI) boards. HDI boards feature more layers in smaller footprints, while rigid-flex boards utilize flexible PCBs to connect multiple HDI sections, enabling three-dimensional configurations within devices.
A significant advancement is the ‘any layer HDI’ technology, which allows connections between any circuit layers, offering greater design flexibility and further miniaturization. Additionally, Substrate-Like PCBs blend PCB and integrated circuit packaging technologies, pushing the boundaries of circuit density and performance.
Challenges in PCB Production # With each new generation, PCBs become smaller and more complex, requiring precise control over line width and spacing. Each layer of a PCB may demand unique process parameters, such as specific flow rates and spray pressures. To ensure reliability and repeatability, manufacturers employ variable frequency drives (VFDs) to control pumps and continuously monitor and adjust process parameters for stability.
Advanced Process Controls and Automation # Modern PCB manufacturing relies heavily on automation to manage the multitude of variables in each production step. However, automation alone is not sufficient. Continuous feedback systems are essential to detect deviations—such as changes in spray pressure due to a malfunctioning nozzle—and alert operators or control centers promptly. This feedback loop minimizes production losses and maintains product quality.
Automated PCB Production PCB Manufacturing Environment Production Environment Improvements # Traditionally, PCB factories used open plating tanks, exposing workers to corrosive fumes. Today, most processes occur within enclosed or environmentally controlled equipment, significantly improving workplace safety. As circuit features shrink, controlling dust and maintaining a clean environment become critical. Modern facilities are climate-controlled, with limited on-site personnel to reduce contamination and heat. Equipment is designed for reliability and leak-free operation, supporting preventive maintenance and minimizing downtime.
Strategies for Cost Competitiveness # The PCB market is highly competitive, making cost control and high yield rates essential. Manufacturers can enhance competitiveness through several strategies:
Utilize High-Efficiency Equipment: Energy efficiency is a key focus. Since production lines integrate various technologies—pumps, heat exchangers, conveyors—collaboration with system designers and component manufacturers is vital to identify energy-saving opportunities.
Consider Life-Cycle Costs (LCC): Evaluating the total cost of equipment over its lifetime—including purchase, installation, operation, maintenance, downtime, and decommissioning—provides a clearer picture of long-term value. For example, operational costs often dominate the LCC of chemical pumps, with maintenance and downtime also playing significant roles.
Prioritize Equipment Durability: PCB process equipment typically has an average lifecycle of about eight years. Components that match or exceed this lifespan, such as durable chemical pumps, offer better value by reducing replacement frequency and associated costs.
Related Solutions and Further Information # With extensive experience and customization capabilities, we assist companies in identifying the most suitable solutions for their PCB manufacturing needs. For more details or tailored advice, please contact us.

Ensuring Pump Reliability with Monitoring and Protection Solutions # The pump serves as the core of any circulating or fluid transfer system, playing a vital role in maintaining operational efficiency. Given the presence of numerous moving parts, it is essential not only to have a robust structural design but also to implement effective monitoring and protection mechanisms. This approach helps prevent abnormal operations and detects early signs of wear, ultimately extending the lifespan of the equipment and reducing costly downtime.
The Importance of Pump Protection # Pumps are susceptible to various operational risks, including overloading and dry running. Without adequate protection, these issues can lead to significant damage, production interruptions, and increased maintenance costs. To address these challenges, we offer two specialized devices designed to enhance pump safety and reliability:
DRP-D Dry Run Protector: This basic device monitors the current drawn by the motor, identifying abnormal loading conditions. By setting thresholds for both over-current and under-current, the DRP-D protects the motor from overloading and the pump from running dry or decoupling. This proactive approach helps prevent damage and minimizes the risk of extended production downtime.
AVF-M Advanced Pump Monitor: Tailored for our canned motor pump series, the AVF-M goes beyond current monitoring. It tracks additional parameters to provide a comprehensive assessment of pump health, ensuring early detection of potential issues and supporting predictive maintenance strategies.
Product Highlight: Overload and Dry-Run Protector (DRP-D) # Overload and Dry-Run Protector
The DRP-D pump protector system is a critical component within any pumping setup. Its primary function is to monitor pump loading, providing dual protection:
Over-current protection: Shields the motor from excessive loads. Under-current protection: Detects dry-run conditions and decoupling, safeguarding the pump from potential damage. By integrating the DRP-D, facilities can significantly reduce the risk of unplanned downtime and maintain smooth, uninterrupted operations.
